title: The Aave revenue-share clock stops when Spark's activity falls below a floor, so the term is measured in productive time
content:
Both revenue-share regimes contain the same unusual clause. Pre-launch (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.2.3.1): if less than 100 million Dai is borrowed, "accrual towards the virtual revenue share payments are paused... **and the counting down of the revenue share duration is paused**." Post-launch (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.2.3.2): if Spark generates less than 1 million Dai per year in income, the same two things pause together, resuming when income recovers.

The duration is two years from September 25th, 2023 — but only two years of *qualifying activity*. Dormant periods do not count against it.

Without the second half of the clause, the first half would be an invitation. A fixed calendar term plus an activity-gated accrual means the cheapest way to extinguish the obligation is to stay below the threshold until the clock runs out: pause accrual, let the calendar do the work, and emerge two years later owing nothing. Suppressing borrowing volume for a period is well within a protocol's control — a rate change would do it.

Pausing the countdown closes that door completely. Aave's entitlement is denominated in a quantity of Spark's *successful operation*, not in elapsed time, so shrinking the business only defers the payment rather than avoiding it. There is no strategy that ends the obligation except paying it out through genuine activity.

The generalizable point: whenever a time-limited obligation is gated on a performance threshold, the term must be measured in gated time too, or the gate becomes the escape hatch.
description: Below 100M Dai borrowed pre-launch or 1M Dai/year income after, both accrual and the countdown of the two-year duration pause — Spark cannot shrink its way out of the obligation.
